items.title: Estimating Implicit Regularization in Deep Learning
items.summary: arXiv:2605.05436v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Deep learning systems are known to exhibit implicit regularization (alt. implicit bias), favoring simple solutions instead of merely minimizing the loss function. In some cases, we can analytically derive the implicit regularization -- connecting it to an equivalent penalty that augments the learning objective. However, modern deep learning systems are complex, carrying modifications to the training procedure and architecture (e.g. early stopping, minibatching, dropout) whose effects are not always directly interpretable. Although estimating the resulting implicit regularization could aid theorists in algorithm design and practitioners in interpreting their hyperparameter choices, this problem has received little direct attention. It is also tractable: regularization makes weight updates deviate from loss gradients, promising a signal for identifying implicit bias. Here we provide gradient matching methods that can be used to empirically estimate the implicit regularization. Our method works on networks with known regularization, recovering popular explicit penalties like $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$. It also replicates known implicit effects, like the quadratic weight penalty induced by early stopping in gradient descent, demonstrating that it can be used to test theories of implicit regularization. Crucially, because our method is empirical, it can handle implicit regularization in arbitrary networks. We demonstrate this use by characterizing implicit $\ell_2$ effects of dropout in deep networks. Our work shows that practitioners can use gradient matching to understand regularization in networks with implicit biases that are too complicated to derive analytically.

items.title: Factual recall in linear associative memories: sharp asymptotics and mechanistic insights
items.summary: arXiv:2605.10795v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large language models excel at factual recall, yet the fundamental limits of storing input--output associations with neural networks remain unclear. We study these limits in a minimal setting: a linear associative memory that maps $p$ input embeddings in $\mathbb{R}^d$ to their $d$-dimensional targets via a linear layer, requiring each mapped input to score its own target above all other outputs. Since all inputs compete for the same outputs, these constraints are strongly correlated, which makes the storage capacity $p_c$ --- the largest number of associations that can be stored --- hard to characterise. We address this in three steps. First, we introduce a decoupled model, in which each input competes with its own independent set of outputs, and provide numerical and analytical evidence that it is equivalent to the original model, both in capacity and in the structure of the learnt solution. Second, using tools from statistical physics, we show that the decoupled model has capacity $p_c \log p_c / d^2 = 1/2$, extend this computation to linear two-layer networks, and go beyond the capacity by predicting the spectrum of the learnt weights and the storage mechanism. The latter explains how the optimal solution outperforms a na\"ive Hebbian rule: rather than boosting input--output alignments with broad fluctuations, it raises the correct scores just above the extreme-value threshold set by the competing outputs. Third, we prove the decoupled model's capacity thresholds rigorously, including in the non-convex two-layer case; combined with a recent proof for the original model, this shows that both models have the same capacity for full-rank weights. These findings give a sharp characterisation of factual storage in linear networks, and suggest decoupling as a general tool for memorisation and learning problems in which each input must be matched to one of an extensive number of outputs.

items.summary: arXiv:2605.11221v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Predictive models in medicinal chemistry depend on structured assay data locked in primary publications. This bottleneck is acute in targeted protein degradation (TPD), where each assay record must combine compound identity, degradation target, recruiter, assay context, and endpoint values reported across sections, tables, and supplementary files. With only seven annotated molecular glue publications, the workflow achieved record-level $F_1 = 0.98$ and transferred to proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) by terminology substitution alone ($F_1 \geq 0.93$). The resulting database, AutoTPD, contained 81% and 92% more molecular glue and PROTAC records than standardized reference datasets; expert audits found 92/100 and 33/40 new records to be correct. Applying the workflow to eligible PubMed Central open-access literature added 4,483 records from 598 publications, yielding AutoTPD+, a public, versioned database of 7,622 TPD records, including degradation assay measurements, designed for monthly updates. In a controlled surrogate model comparison, PROTAC degradation activity models trained on AutoTPD+ saw a 8.9-18.2% error reduction relative to models trained on the original PROTAC-DB data.

items.title: EPIC: Efficient Predicate-Guided Inference-Time Control for Compositional Text-to-Image Generation
items.summary: arXiv:2605.11722v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recent text-to-image (T2I) generators can synthesize realistic images, but still struggle with compositional prompts involving multiple objects, counts, attributes, and relations. We introduce EPIC (Efficient Predicate-Guided Inference-Time Control), a training-free inference-time refinement framework for compositional T2I generation. EPIC casts refinement as predicate-guided search: it parses the original prompt once into a visual program of object variables and typed predicates, then verifies each candidate image against this program using visual evidence extracted from that image. A candidate is judged to satisfy the prompt when all predicates pass; otherwise, unmet predicates guide the next step, routing localized failures to targeted editing and layout-level or persistent failures to resampling. On GenEval2, EPIC improves the prompt-level Soft-TIFA GM score from 34.16% for single-pass generation to 71.46%. With the same generator, editor, and image-model execution budget, EPIC outperforms the strongest baseline by 19.23 points. items.title: Bridging the Modality Bottleneck in Pathology MIL through Molecularly Guided Feature Adaptation
items.summary: arXiv:2605.16392v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Multiple instance learning (MIL) is the dominant framework for whole-slide image analysis in computational pathology, typically combining a frozen patch encoder, a projection layer, and a slide-level aggregator. While encoders and aggregators have been extensively studied, the projection layer remains a largely morphology-only bottleneck. This limits endpoints such as biomarker status and survival, which are governed by a molecular state that is not fully captured by H&E morphology. We introduce Molecularly Informed Staining Transform (MIST), a plug-in replacement for the MIL projection layer that uses paired spatial transcriptomics only during training to construct virtual molecular stains. MIST clusters gene expression profiles into cross-modal prototypes, anchors them in the frozen foundation model feature space, and uses them to reorganize H&E patch features along molecularly guided axes. It requires no transcriptomics at inference and can be inserted before standard MIL aggregators. We evaluate MIST across 23 downstream tasks and 8 MIL aggregators. MIST improves 240 of 256 configurations over the standard projection layer, with an average gain of +3.5%, observed consistently across endpoint types: +5.2% on survival prediction, +3.3% on tissue subtyping, and +2.6% on biomarker prediction. Ablations confirm that gene-derived prototypes are the primary source of the gains, while spatial, biological, and pathological analyses show that cross-modal prototype affinities capture spatially coherent molecular programs from H&E alone.

items.title: Distill to Think, Foresee to Act: Cognitive-Physical Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Driving
items.summary: arXiv:2605.21139v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Current end-to-end autonomous driving models are fundamentally constrained by the behavioral cloning ceiling of imitation learning. While reinforcement learning offers a path to smarter autonomy, it demands two missing pieces of infrastructure: (1) a cognitive foundation that understands traffic semantics and driving intent, and (2) a foresighted physical environment that can anticipate the consequences of candidate actions. To this end, we propose CoPhy, a CognitivePhysical reinforcement learning framework for autonomous driving. To distill to think, we distill VLM knowledge into the BEV encoder and then discard the VLM entirely, retaining cognitive ability at zero inference cost while releasing the cognitive channel as a pluggable interface for optional human language commands. To foresee to act, we build an auto-regressive BEV world model that explicitly predicts future semantic maps conditioned on candidate actions, serving as an interpretable physical sandbox from which safety metrics are directly derived. Built upon this dual infrastructure, we optimize the driving policy via GRPO with a novel dual-reward mechanism: a physical reward derived from BEV rollouts enforces hard safety constraints, while a cognitive reward from a language-aligned scorer ensures intent compliance. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CoPhy not only achieves state-of-the-art results on NAVSIM v1 and v2 benchmarks, but also enables safer driving via cognitively informed scene compliance and flexible intent control through user-defined language instructions. items.title: A Rigorous, Tractable Measure of Model Complexity
items.summary: arXiv:2605.21167v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: An accurate assessment of a model's complexity is crucial for topics such as interpretation, generalization, and model selection. However, existing complexity measures either rely on heuristic assumptions or are computationally prohibitive. In this paper, we present a mathematically rigorous yet easy-to-compute measure of model complexity that is based on the similarities between feature vectors for different inputs. It is thus well-defined for any parametric model (via NTK feature generalization) and for kernel-based non-parametric models (via the induced kernel). We prove that our measure of complexity generalizes model-specific complexity measures, including polynomial degree (for polynomial regression), kernel length scale (for Mat\'ern kernels), number of neighbors (for k-nearest neighbors), number of splits (for decision trees), and number of trees (for random forests). We also use our measure to obtain new insights into the double descent phenomenon for random Fourier features, random forests, neural networks, and gradient boosting.

items.summary: arXiv:2605.28516v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Simulation-based inference with neural posterior estimation (NPE) often yields overconfident and unreliable posteriors under limited simulation budgets. To address this, we propose DRO-NPE, a distributionally robust approach that replaces the standard NPE objective with a worst-case loss over a Wasserstein ambiguity set. We introduce KL-based metrics for miscoverage and miscalibration, and use these to show that the DRO-NPE objective controls overfitting and reduces posterior overconfidence. Our method is tractable, parallelisable, and readily integrates with standard normalising flows. Across benchmark SBI tasks, DRO-NPE consistently improves coverage and calibration, while narrowing the gap between empirical and population NPE loss, leading to more reliable inference in low-simulation regimes.

items.title: Diffusion Models Observe Only Gradients: A Geometric Perspective on Score Matching Errors
items.summary: arXiv:2606.06179v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Score-based diffusion models are typically trained by minimizing the $L^2$ score matching error, and standard theoretical analyses rely on this quantity to bound the sampling discrepancy between the learned and target distributions. Recent work has shown that the score admits an orthogonal decomposition into gradient and solenoidal components in which only the gradient part matters for exact sampling. We apply this decomposition to the score error of trained models and study its quantitative consequences. Since only the gradient component of the error enters the marginal Fokker-Planck dynamics, a model can incur arbitrarily large $L^2$ score error while perfectly matching the target. Starting from this observation, we present three results. First, we derive an upper bound on the Kullback-Leibler divergence that depends only on the observable gradient component of the error. It tightens the standard Girsanov bound for generic score networks and identifies that bound's looseness as the cost of working with path-space rather than marginal-space dynamics. Second, we prove that no non-trivial function of the $L^2$ score error can uniformly lower bound any divergence between the learned and target distributions. Third, we give an estimator of the gradient component, computable from denoising score matching residuals via a dual Sobolev identity, which empirically correlates substantially better with sample quality than the full $L^2$ error.

items.title: Anchor PCA
items.summary: arXiv:2606.06233v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Principal component analysis (PCA) is one of the most widely used unsupervised dimension reduction techniques. We study PCA for data from multiple related domains. Since principal components generally differ across domains, one way to obtain a shared low-rank embedding is to perform PCA on the pooled data. However, this approach can focus on spurious directions that exhibit high variation in only a few domains. To find a robust embedding that still explains most variance in unseen but similar domains, we propose instead to focus on shared directions of variation. To this end, we introduce Anchor PCA which trades off overall explained variance with agreement between the shared and domain-specific low-rank embeddings. Anchor PCA amounts to PCA on a modified target matrix and thus can be solved efficiently. Moreover, we show that Anchor PCA recovers a maximal invariant subspace and admits a minimax reconstruction interpretation under bounded domain-specific covariance inflations. On simulated and real-world data with temporal distribution shift, we demonstrate, respectively, that Anchor PCA recovers the maximal invariant subspace and yields embeddings that explain more variance on unseen domains than the pooling baseline and a worst-case alternative. Taken together, these findings establish Anchor PCA as a promising approach to robust unsupervised dimension reduction from multi-domain data.

items.title: Large-scale empirical tuning and comparison of default optimizers for variational inference
items.summary: arXiv:2606.07841v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Black-box variational inference (BBVI) is a methodology for posterior approximation that relies on stochastic optimization. In practice, the stochastic optimizers underpinning BBVI generally require extensive problem-specific tuning, which undermines its promise as a truly "black box" inference algorithm. However, over the past decade, many new adaptive stochastic optimization algorithms have been developed that reduce or remove entirely the need for tuning. In this work, we investigate this new collection of adaptive methods in the context of BBVI, with the goal of establishing the current state of the art in tuning-free optimization-based inference. In particular, we present a large-scale empirical evaluation of 56 stochastic gradient-based optimization algorithms applied to 1092 Bayesian inference optimization problems, involving over 550,000 individual optimization runs and 15 core-years of compute. The optimization algorithms we evaluate are chosen to represent a wide spectrum of recent approaches and the benchmark problems are chosen to span a range of difficulty, with posterior target dimension 1-10^4, condition number 1-10^8, and a range of variational families. Our results show that no single method dominates, but running a selection of 5 algorithms suffices to reliably get close to the best-possible observed performance. We thus provide a strong baseline for applications where expert tuning is not possible and for comparison when developing new stochastic optimization algorithms.

items.title: Driving Video Retrieval for Complex Queries with Structured Grounding
items.summary: arXiv:2606.09109v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Video retrieval at scale is central to data curation and safety validation in autonomous driving, where users want to find not only scenes but also dynamic events such as cut-ins and hard braking. Existing vision-language and keyword-based retrieval methods often miss these events because the relevant motion may not be explicitly described in text or captured by lexical overlap. Rule-based retrieval can encode such events more directly, but it is brittle: generated or hand-written rules often fail when their assumptions do not match real driving data. We propose STRIVE-D, a data-calibrated retrieval framework for driving videos. It uses weakly labeled in-domain videos to estimate when a query rule is reliable, adapt rules that mismatch observed data, and fuse calibrated rule scores with vision-language and keyword-based retrieval signals. Across three driving benchmarks, including newly released human-annotated event data on DrivingDojo, STRIVE-D delivers up to 84% relative improvement in top-1 accuracy over state-of-the-art methods.

items.title: Teaching Diffusion to Speculate Left-to-Right
items.summary: arXiv:2606.11552v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) achieve remarkable performance across a wide range of tasks, but their autoregressive decoding process incurs substantial inference costs due to inherently sequential token generation. Speculative decoding addresses this bottleneck by employing a lightweight draft model to propose multiple future tokens that are subsequently verified in parallel by a larger target model. Recent work has demonstrated that diffusion language models are well suited for this setting, as they can generate entire blocks of draft tokens in parallel and thereby alleviate the sequential constraints of autoregressive drafting. A subtlety of this regime is that block-diffusion drafters generate tokens bidirectionally within a block, whereas verification is performed by an autoregressive target model that evaluates tokens in a strictly left-to-right manner, leaving a gap between the symmetric training-time objective and the asymmetric verification-time reward. In this work, we offer an empirical analysis of three training-time interventions that narrow this gap: token positional weighting, a first-error focal loss that targets the position that breaks the accepted prefix within each block, and a chain loss term that substitutes a differentiable surrogate for the expected accepted length. The three interventions act along orthogonal axes (position, block-conditional first error, joint prefix) and compose additively; they are likewise orthogonal to test-time alignment mechanisms such as multi-draft self-selection, with which they can in principle be combined. Across four target models and six reasoning, code, and dialogue benchmarks, the three interventions raise accepted draft length by 21-76% per benchmark over a position-uniform baseline, without adding additional forward passes and without changing the inference pipeline or the rejection-sampling exactness contract.

items.summary: arXiv:2606.13133v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recently, Antoniadis et al. We develop a learning-augmented algorithm for the makespan minimization problem on unrelated machines, denoted by $R\|C_{\max}$. By using predictions of heavy job assignments, we achieve a polynomial-time $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximation for accurate predictions that smoothly degrades to a worst-case 2-approximation as the error increases. items.title: Machine-learned particle flow as a foundation model for collider physics
items.summary: arXiv:2606.14373v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The workflow from particle collision to physics analysis passes through a series of reconstruction steps that are traditionally modular and disconnected, with no shared representation linking low-level detector data to high-level analysis tasks. We show that casting event reconstruction as a machine learning problem naturally produces such a shared representation. We repurpose a machine learning model trained for particle-flow reconstruction (MLPF) to perform three distinct analysis tasks: jet flavor identification, jet energy regression, and missing momentum regression. By appending the per-particle latent representations learned during reconstruction as additional input features, we substantially improve over baselines that use conventional particle-level features alone. We further demonstrate that a single linear layer trained using only the latent representations achieves competitive performance against state-of-the-art baseline architectures, and outperforms the baseline for missing momentum regression with approximately 35 times fewer parameters. These results demonstrate that the latent representations learned during reconstruction encode essential physics information needed for downstream analysis, establishing MLPF as a foundation model and offering a concrete step toward an end-to-end pipeline from detector data to physics analysis.

items.title: AutoDex: An Automated Real-World System for Dexterous Grasping Data Collection
items.summary: arXiv:2606.23689v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Scaling real-world dexterous-grasp data collection is limited by the sustained human effort required to operate the robot, verify grasp outcomes, and reset objects between trials. Simulation can generate grasp candidates at scale, but their success on hardware remains uncertain. We present AutoDex, a system that collects real-world dexterous-grasp data without continuous human operation. Given generated grasp candidates, AutoDex plans and executes grasps, labels their outcomes, and resets the object to continue collection across stable poses. Multi-view object tracking supports labeling under hand-object occlusion, while residual-torque collision monitoring and pose-directed reset enable the loop to operate without continuous human supervision. Using AutoDex, we collect over 3,500 grasp trials across 100 objects with Allegro and Inspire hands, recording both successes and failures together with synchronized visual observations and robot states. AutoDex reduces human effort by more than an order of magnitude, requiring an estimated 0.2 human-hours to collect 500 trajectories compared with 9.3 for teleoperation. As AutoDex collects trials, it builds a library of physically validated grasps for subsequent execution. In new object placements and obstacle configurations, retrieval from this library achieves 76% success, compared with 34% for candidates screened only in simulation. Code and data are available at https://snuvclab.github.io/AutoDex/.

items.title: Kriging and Neural Network models for pressure losses across perforated plates
items.summary: arXiv:2606.29628v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, two novel data-driven models based on Kriging and neural networks (NN) are proposed to predict pressure losses across perforated plates with circular perforations in turbulent flows. The models are developed using two sets of experimental data available in the literature. The predictive performance of the proposed models is assessed and compared against widely used empirical formulae. It is found that the proposed models consistently outperform existing empirical models for most perforated plate configurations contained in the experimental datasets. Besides, the predicted pressure losses generally show good agreement with experimental measurements, demonstrating that data-driven approaches based on Kriging and NN provide a feasible framework for modelling pressure losses across perforated plates. Overall, both approaches are promising, despite being trained on a relatively limited amount of experimental data, owing to the scarcity of measurements reported in the literature. To demonstrate the applicability of the proposed models in numerical simulations, two-dimensional channel flows are simulated using the Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes (RANS) equations, in which the new pressure-loss models are implemented as a source term in the momentum equations. The RANS predictions are insensitive to mesh resolution and the number of cells used to represent the perforated plate, and they agree well with the model predictions, confirming the applicability of the proposed approaches to practical computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations.

OLIVE couples masked latent prediction and waveform reconstruction through a functional separation within a single encoder: reconstruction constrains early encoder features to retain signal-level information, while masked latent prediction shapes later contextual representations for robust downstream performance, with waveform view augmentations defining the invariances they learn. To the best of our knowledge, OLIVE is the first speech SSL model that directly reconstructs waveforms, retains its vocoder after pre-training, and remains competitive on discriminative tasks. Adding reconstruction largely preserves the speech recognition performance of masked latent prediction alone, while improving waveform reconstruction and speaker tasks. Adding waveform mixup and gain augmentations provides a controllable way to shift the representations further toward speaker, generation, and reconstruction tasks, while remaining competitive on recognition and semantic tasks.

items.title: AbsoluteDegradation: A Physics-Inspired Synthetic Film-Degradation Pipeline and Archival Film Restoration Benchmark
items.summary: arXiv:2607.02131v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Restoring archival film remains a fundamentally challenging problem due to the absence of paired training data and the lack of standardized evaluation benchmarks. Pristine versions of deteriorated footage are physically unrecoverable, requiring supervised methods to rely on synthetic data that often fail to capture the complex, temporally coherent nature of real film degradation. At the same time, existing real-world datasets are limited in scale, quality, and accessibility, hindering reliable evaluation and fair comparison across methods. We address both limitations with AbsoluteDegradation, a physics-inspired, modular pipeline for synthesizing realistic film degradations, and a new large-scale archival benchmark. The proposed pipeline models the analog-to-digital process as a structured composition of artifact families, incorporating signal-dependent grain, parametric scratches, and temporally coherent camera motion, enabling controlled generation of diverse degradation regimes. In parallel, we introduce a curated dataset of 81,576 high-resolution frames sourced from real archival footage, designed for consistent evaluation under real-world conditions. Together, these contributions provide a unified framework for training and benchmarking restoration models. Experiments across six restoration architectures, evaluated with no-reference image quality metrics, clip-level temporal quality assessment, and a blinded human preference study (93 raters, 1,395 trials), show that models trained with AbsoluteDegradation generalize better to real-world footage: human raters preferred them in 64.7% of comparisons and for every evaluated architecture. The proposed benchmark also reveals systematic failure modes of current methods and of no-reference metrics. We hope this work establishes a foundation for reproducible and domain-authentic evaluation in archival film restoration.

items.title: TTHE: Test-Time Harness Evolution
items.summary: arXiv:2607.08124v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The behavior of an LLM agent is determined not only by the underlying model, but also by its harness: the executable program that constructs context, invokes tools, verifies intermediate results, and recovers from failures. Existing approaches typically optimize harnesses on training or development data and freeze the resulting programs at test time, limiting adaptation to shifts in task distributions, failure modes, and tool interactions. We ask whether the harness can instead be optimized during evaluation using unlabeled execution traces. We introduce Test-Time Harness Evolution (TTHE), which treats the executable harness as the state of test-time adaptation. On each unlabeled test batch, TTHE iteratively evolves a population of candidate harnesses through agentic proposers that reason over execution traces and explore diverse edit directions. A judge selects a candidate using execution traces and execution-derived proxy signals. The selected harness determines the current batch's outputs and initializes adaptation on the next. Crucially, the solver, proposers, and judge operate through different harnesses around the same frozen LLM, without weight updates, access to final-answer labels, or a separately trained adaptation model. These results recast test-time adaptation for LLM agents as evolution over executable control programs and identify execution-derived proxy reliability as a central challenge for robust unsupervised agent improvement.

items.title: Efficient Robust Learning at the Information-Theoretic Limit
items.summary: arXiv:2609.17655v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In an important recent work, Blanc (2026) gave an algorithm for robustly learning Boolean concept classes with respect to a fixed distribution that outputs a (randomized) classifier achieving the optimal error of $\eta + \varepsilon$ where $\eta$ is the noise rate. In contrast, it is well known that deterministic hypotheses cannot achieve error less than $2\eta + \varepsilon$. Blanc's algorithm is computationally inefficient, and the main problem left open in his work is to find a polynomial-time algorithm given access to an oracle for empirical risk minimization (ERM). Here we resolve this problem and give such an algorithm. Additionally, we give an efficient algorithm (no ERM oracle required) for robustly learning any function class that admits low-degree polynomial approximators with respect to hypercontractive distributions. This captures basic settings including halfspaces with respect to Gaussian marginals. Our techniques make new connections to various types of online convex optimization algorithms. As a surprising consequence, we show that efficient SQ learnability in the agnostic setting implies efficient learning with contamination (with respect to Gaussians or uniform over the hypercube).

items.title: MMAP: Multimodal Missing-Aware Pretraining for Longitudinal Alzheimer's Prediction
items.summary: arXiv:2609.26617v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Clinical decision making heavily relies on predicting the disease progression trajectory by seeking to understand patient's health status which is characterised by multimodal medical data. AI holds great potential for learning useful representations from multimodal medical data to predict disease progression and aid clinical decision making. However, development of predictive AI models is constrained by missing modalities and incomplete tabular data frequently occurring in medical datasets. In addition, disease labels alone may only provide limited supervisory signals for learning representations from high-dimensional multimodal data. Here, we present MMAP, a novel Multimodal Missing-aware Alignment Pretraining method for learning image-tabular representations from incomplete data. An image encoder is pretrained with efficient sigmoid contrastive learning combined with generative reconstruction. A tabular encoder is built upon a tabular foundation model. A missing token generator enables the two encoders to take incomplete data as input, enabling the model to be robust against missing modalities, either with missing images or missing tabular data. We evaluate the clinical usefulness of the learnt multimodal representations on two challenging longitudinal clinical tasks for Alzheimer's disease: predicting disease stage conversion and predicting amyloid status. The proposed method outperforms strong multimodal and unimodal baselines.

items.summary: arXiv:2609.30809v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the use of neural network solvers for infinity and $p$-Laplace problems, which are fundamental in nonlinear analysis and have practical applications. Our approach employs Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) and Deep Operator Networks (DeepONets) to address computational challenges associated with large $p$ values, ranging from $2$ to $1000$, on various 2D and 3D domains. Our method offers advantages over traditional physics-based solvers, especially in three dimensions where mesh-based solvers become very costly for these problems. We also establish conditional convergence results for PINN approximations of both problems and a universal approximation result for DeepONet on the parametric $p$-Poisson problem. We demonstrate the effectiveness of these neural network solvers through numerical experiments and compare their performance with conventional methods.

items.title: Schr\"odinger--F\"ollmer Actor--Critic: Diffusion Policy Improvement with Finite-Sample Analysis
items.summary: arXiv:2609.33239v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Diffusion policies represent multimodal action distributions, but a $Q$-weighted update does not specify how to sample from the resulting target distribution. We propose Schr\"odinger--F\"ollmer Actor--Critic (SFAC), an offline-to-online reinforcement learning (RL) method for Kullback--Leibler (KL)-regularized policy improvement through conditional diffusion. A minimax Bellman critic estimates the action-value function, which defines an exponentially tilted target policy. A Doob $h$-transform expresses this update as a correction to the reference diffusion drift. The target drift is a weighted conditional mean of Brownian-bridge labels. We fit it by weighted regression using endpoints from the current policy and pointwise action-value evaluations. In the small-update regime, the KL-regularized update follows the natural policy-gradient direction, and the Doob correction represents the same local change in the space of diffusion drifts. Under suitable conditions, we derive finite-sample bounds that separate the errors from critic estimation, weighted neural drift regression, and diffusion discretization through a reverse-KL actor bound. The average-performance bound depends explicitly on the comparison coefficients over the policy iterations. Synthetic experiments assess approximation to prescribed tilted targets and sensitivity to the diffusion-step count. Across six offline-to-online continuous-control tasks, the $Q$-guided bridge-regression implementation achieves higher performance than its offline initialization after online policy improvement.

items.title: Dynamic Quadtree Tokenization and Transformer for Adaptive Mesh PDE Forecasting
items.summary: arXiv:2610.04044v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The quadratic attention cost of Vision Transformers (ViTs) forces a trade-off between spatial resolution and rollout horizon, particularly for fine-scale PDEs where shocks, reaction fronts, and material interfaces occupy small, evolving regions of the domain. Conventional neural surrogates also lack mechanisms to adapt resolution dynamically. We propose WAMRViT, a ViT that tokenizes inputs as balanced quadtrees using a wavelet-inspired refinement criterion, jointly encodes position and refinement level with 3D rotary positional embeddings, and regrids in cell space during inference for stable long-horizon rollouts. A multi-scale variant retains each leaf at its native source resolution and lets the model learn across resolution levels. Unlike fixed-budget adaptive-tokenization methods, WAMRViT imposes no predetermined token count and supports fully adaptive topology throughout autoregressive rollout. To our knowledge, it is the first machine-learning surrogate to natively tokenize multi-level Adaptive Mesh Refinement (AMR) data. On uniform-grid benchmarks, uniform-patch WAMRViT improves finest-level region-of-interest VRMSE over a finest-patch uniform ViT while using substantially fewer tokens. The multi-scale variant achieves the lowest first-step full-field RMSE and VRMSE on both benchmarks and improves rollout-averaged full-field and refined-region accuracy at long horizons. With parallelized regridding, its end-to-end rollout cost lies between finest-patch and approximately token-matched coarser-patch ViTs. On a complex AMR combustion problem whose finest features cannot be represented natively by the evaluated uniform-grid baselines, WAMRViT operates on adaptive cells built from the simulator hierarchy and substantially reduces finest-level error at matched transformer capacity. items.title: Product Monte Carlo: Expectation Under a Product of Densities
items.summary: arXiv:2610.12702v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Aggregating independently computed sub-sample inferences is a well-known challenge in large-scale Bayesian computation, federated learning, and opinion pooling. The core problem is to approximate a distribution whose density is proportional to a product of individual densities. We propose Product Monte Carlo (PMC), an algorithm for computing arbitrary expectations under a product of densities using only Monte Carlo draws from individual densities. We turn the intractable product expectation into a regression problem by expressing it through a family of computable conditional expectations. Besides the point estimate, our fully Bayesian regression formulation provides coherent uncertainty quantification and principled diagnostics. We establish theoretical guarantees on consistency and characterize convergence rates for the PMC estimator. Across simulated and real-data experiments varying the number, dimensionality, and heterogeneity of the component distributions, PMC achieves higher estimation accuracy, better-calibrated uncertainty coverage, and improved scalability at a lower computational cost than existing methods. In addition, PMC requires no density evaluation, making it applicable to simulation-based inference, as we demonstrate in an application with protein images.

items.title: Neuromorphic Decoding and Dynamical Image Reconstruction from Populations of Spiking Retinal Ganglion Cells
items.summary: arXiv:2610.17154v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Decoding visual stimuli from the spiking activity of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) informs both our understanding of the retinal code and the design of visual prostheses. Natural vision is dynamic, yet state-of-the-art decoders mostly reconstruct single frames with artificial neural networks that process dense, continuous-valued signals rather than the retina's sparse, asynchronous spikes. We asked whether dynamic scenes can be reconstructed and tracked entirely within the spike domain, and at what computational cost. We built an end-to-end spiking neural network (SNN) whose neurons integrate the recorded RGC spikes over time. Populations of up to 1836 RGCs were recorded ex vivo from mouse retina on high-density microelectrode arrays while flashed images, moving bars, drifting gratings and randomly moving handwritten digits were presented. For moving digits, one shared spiking encoder fed two readouts, one reconstructing the image and one decoding the digit's position. Compute energy was estimated from counted synaptic operations. The SNN decoded what and where at once. It reconstructed the stimuli with a structural similarity (SSIM) of up to 0.93, refining the reconstruction as spikes accumulated, and tracked a randomly moving target with a mean error of 1.33 pixels on a $32\times32$ grid. Its fidelity nearly matched that of the best of 17 larger spiking and artificial decoders (5.9 million to 1.7 billion parameters, versus 5.4 million), and at a mean firing rate of 14.2% it needed an estimated $\sim$70-fold less compute energy than a dense artificial network of the same architecture. Dynamic visual scenes can thus be decoded from retinal population activity in the spike domain, with a compact network and at a compute cost compatible with implantable and wearable neural interfaces, supporting spike-native decoders for visual prostheses.

items.title: FutureLift: Lifting Trajectory Proposals into Bidirectional Future Graphs for Motion Forecasting
items.summary: arXiv:2610.22215v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Accurate motion prediction is critical for safe autonomous driving, yet even strong forecasters leave residual errors in their multimodal proposals. Existing refiners compress complete proposals or update their segments sequentially, preventing the full proposed future from serving as explicit relational context for correction. We introduce FutureLift, a backbone-agnostic refiner that represents each multimodal proposal as a heterogeneous future graph, with spatially grounded temporal nodes connected to agent histories, map elements, alternative modes, and, for joint prediction, other agents future trajectories. Bidirectional temporal edges allow later evidence to revise earlier segments in a single pass, and the updated nodes predict residual coordinate and confidence corrections. Requiring only proposals, scores, and scene context, FutureLift provides a common refinement interface for structurally different forecasting backbones. On Argoverse2 and the Waymo Open Motion Dataset, it consistently improves frozen proposals and outperforms native and specialized refiners across marginal and joint forecasting. On the WOMD motion-prediction leaderboard, FutureLift ranks first in minADE (0.5049m) and minFDE (0.9942m) among the compared standard-input methods, without LiDAR or ensembling, while achieving a competitive 0.4874 Soft mAP.

items.title: Where Prefill Expert Reduction Hurts MoE Models: A Few Prompt Tokens Carry Most of the Short-Answer F1 Loss
items.summary: arXiv:2610.22454v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Running prompt tokens through fewer routed experts during prefill makes mixture-of-experts (MoE) serving cheaper, but what it damages has not been measured. We locate the damage with token-, layer- and attention-path interventions in four MoE families on short-answer question answering. At half the experts the F1 loss is mostly answer form: the model still finds the answer but no longer answers briefly. The loss is made at a few tokens: the two chat-template tokens before the answer in Qwen3-30B-A3B, and the first 8-32 tokens, where the instruction sits, in DeepSeek-V2-Lite. Keeping them at full experts removes most of the F1 loss and about half and a fifth of the increase in answer NLL. Reduction changes the first-token sink statistics by less than 4%, and restoring super experts or massive activations recovers at most a quarter of the loss. We then test placement on real prompts with about 4% of tokens at full experts. Putting them on the task interface keeps F1 within one point of the unmodified model, while the same budget scattered in the documents is about 3 points worse in both prespecified primary tests of this comparison. Time to first token falls about 14% on 11K-token prompts.

items.title: FrameScout: Scouting Query-Relevant Frames for Long Video Understanding
items.summary: arXiv:2610.23975v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Long video understanding requires VideoLLMs to answer queries about videos spanning tens of minutes to hours, but such long videos produce far more visual tokens than current VideoLLMs can process. To address this issue, keyframe selectors are proposed to select the most query-relevant frames by computing the similarity between frame and query embeddings. Existing selectors either encode frames independently without temporal context or process chunks in isolation with ranking objectives that are difficult to optimize. To alleviate those limitations, we propose FrameScout with two core designs: (i) a streaming selector architecture that leverages a sliding-window KV cache and successor aggregation to produce temporally-contextualized frame embeddings; (ii) a frame-query contrastive objective that aligns frame and query embeddings in a shared space, directly training the selector to distinguish relevant frames from irrelevant ones. Extensive experiments on three long-video benchmarks and six base VideoLLMs demonstrate that FrameScout consistently achieves state-of-the-art performance. items.title: Probabilistic Meshless Methods on Manifolds
items.summary: arXiv:2610.39855v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Probabilistic meshless methods solve partial differential equations (PDEs) by placing a Gaussian process prior on the solution and conditioning it on the PDE at a finite set of collocation nodes. The posterior provides both an approximation of the solution and a Bayesian quantification of its error. While these methods are well established on Euclidean domains, their extension to manifolds lacks, to our knowledge, any convergence analysis. We extend them to compact manifolds and study their convergence in two settings. First, for known manifolds whose Laplace-Beltrami eigenpairs are available, the prior can be evaluated exactly, but the PDE operator generally cannot be applied to it in closed form. We replace this operator by a standard generalized finite difference discretization on a point cloud sampled from the manifold, and show that the resulting method is consistent at the points of the cloud, at a rate governed by their fill distance. Second, for implicit manifolds, known only through a point cloud, both the prior and the operator must be approximated. We propose a new generalized finite difference scheme with a free stencil radius, and show that it retains the consistency of the standard construction while controlling the growth of its coefficients, and that an appropriate radius yields uniform convergence of the discrete Gram matrix. In both settings, we derive error bounds for the posterior mean which separate the collocation error intrinsic to the method from the error due to approximating the operator and, for implicit manifolds, the prior. Experiments on the circle, the sphere and the flat torus confirm our theoretical claims. On real-world cortical thickness data, our approach attains the accuracy of established discretizations, while conditioning on fewer than a tenth of the observations and providing a credible interval at every vertex.

items.title: Neural Actor--Critic Learning with Minimax Critics and Reflected Langevin Sampling
items.summary: arXiv:2611.03352v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Actor--critic methods rely on critic gradients to improve continuous-action policies, yet finite-sample guarantees must control both value and gradient errors and their propagation through the actor. We develop a neural actor-critic procedure that combines a regularized minimax Bellman estimator over sigmoid networks with a finite reflected Langevin sampler driven by the fitted critic gradient. Under uniform Bellman regularity and covered reset sampling, a positive high-order action-derivative penalty yields value and action-gradient risk bounds with classical nonparametric minimax exponents up to logarithmic factors. We propagate estimation, mixing, discretization, temperature, and policy-iteration errors to obtain return guarantees, with refinements for bounded multimodal potentials and strongly concave regimes. Empirical studies across controlled simulations, logged continuous-control data, and a simulated decision task show favorable performance relative to the considered baselines.

items.title: All Paths All at Once: A Quantum Monte Carlo and Neural Committor Approach to Reaction Pathway Search
items.summary: arXiv:2611.03699v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Locating competing reaction pathways is difficult when potential-energy gradients are unavailable. Here we present tReax_expedition, an energy-only approach combining coupled Monte Carlo exploration, stochastic quench labelling and restrained continuation. Exploration identifies connected states, while continuation resolves candidate channels and records sampled chain maxima. Single-search benchmarks on three two-dimensional potentials recovered an intermediate and competing routes without transition-state guesses. For eight of nine gas-phase reactions on GFN2-xTB, sampled chain maxima differed from independently refined saddle energies by less than 0.76 kJ/mol. Alanine dipeptide instead revealed incomplete conformational relaxation, showing that route connectivity can persist despite structural and energetic errors. Neural committor learning and local straddling-pair sampling connect the resulting paths to transition-region sampling, although molecular shooting diagnostics indicate limited committor calibration. These results show how energy-only exploration and continuation recover candidate pathways, while distinguishing route connectivity from geometric localization, barrier resolution and finite-temperature transition statistics.

items.title: The Complexity of ReLU Network Synthesis from a Parameter Multiset
items.summary: arXiv:2611.04074v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We ask how hard it is to build a ReLU network when its parameter values are given in advance. An instance supplies an appropriate encoding of a target behavior, a multiset of rational numbers, and a bound on the number of neurons (output included). The question is whether one can choose the graph of a ReLU network within the bound, and place the numbers on its edges and biases so that it meets the target. This separates the numbers from the architecture. Matching two labeled examples exactly is already $\mathsf{NP}$-complete, so we ask what changes when the target must hold on every input or on average. Agreeing with a Boolean circuit on every Boolean input is $\Sigma_2^{\mathsf P}$-complete, already for four neurons. Agreeing with a given ReLU network on every real input lies in $\mathsf{DP}$ for every fixed neuron bound and is $\mathsf{DP}$-complete for three neurons. Approximating a ReLU network on the unit cube within absolute error one everywhere is $\Sigma_2^{\mathsf P}$-complete, even with no hidden neurons and all numbers equal and positive. Deciding whether some network has expected squared loss at most a threshold is $\mathsf{NP}^{\mathsf{PP}}$-complete for uniform Boolean inputs. For uniform inputs on the unit cube and for standard Gaussian inputs with a positive threshold, the same holds for two neurons when a positive risk gap, given in binary and possibly exponentially small, separates yes from no instances. Without a gap, the cube version is complete for guessing a polynomial-length string, then comparing a sum of exponentially many rationals with a threshold, all computable in polynomial time from the input and the guess.

items.title: Reading Why: Born-Measured Attention with Exact Word Evidence on Light and Qubits
items.summary: arXiv:2611.05355v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: When a language model answers, we can usually only estimate why. We build a transformer in which every step is a Born measurement - attention $|\langle q|k\rangle|^4$ normalised over each row, a measured product in place of the feed-forward nonlinearity, and a Born readout. With its denominators held at their values for the input, each class probability is a polynomial in the word amplitudes, so its integrated-gradient evidence is computed by a finite quadrature with no quadrature error: the words' contributions sum to the class probability above its no-information share, to $10^{-11}$ or better. On e-SNLI natural language inference, with about 98k parameters outside the embedding, the model reaches $76.98 \pm 0.17$% test accuracy, level with a softmax transformer of the same size ($76.62 \pm 0.36$%). Deleting the word its evidence ranks first changes the answer in 45% of test pairs, out of the 53% any single deletion can change, against 32% for the softmax model explained the same way and 40% by its attention x gradient. Attention can look as much like the words annotators highlighted as the evidence does, yet accounts for the answer less well: deleting the word it ranks first changes the Born Transformer's answer in 32% of pairs. The same weights compile exactly to optoelectronic optics and to qubits, and a coherent attention layer becomes one circuit equal to the model (852 CNOTs on 23 qubits). On IBM's ibm_kingston, reading only the attention overlaps by Hadamard tests, the device gave the model's answers, also when a word was deleted. With calibration circuits as deep as the overlaps, each word's evidence with the device's attention row sums followed the exact evidence (correlations 0.997 and 0.932 on two pairs chosen in advance); where a pair's evidence is a small total of large opposite terms the earlier runs say it does not, and we say why.

items.title: When Disclosure Is Compulsory: Evaluating Ride-Hailing Rebalancing Policies with Self-Interested LLM Driver Agents
items.summary: arXiv:2610.41132v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The EU Platform Work Directive, to be transposed by December 2026, requires ride-hailing platforms to state in plain language the main parameters of their automated decisions and how a worker's behaviour affects them. Such rules are exactly what a large language model (LLM) can read, so drivers will be able to let one decide for them. We compare two main families of rebalancing policy once their rules are public: a reactive policy (R) that sends idle drivers to cover requests just lost, and an anticipatory policy (A) that plans moves on a demand forecast. Each driver is an LLM agent maximizing its own net income, given no rules (N) or the rules at the directive's level of detail (L). We test two LLMs, Claude Haiku 5.5 and Jev, which understand the rules equally well, in a three-zone model and in Manhattan. With the rules disclosed, drivers follow the platform more closely: in Manhattan, the share of relocation offers they decline falls from about four in five to one in four under both policies. Yet the effects differ by policy. For the platform, disclosure costs R 3.7% of its profit in Manhattan, as R now pays for moves drivers used to make for free, while A's profit is unchanged; the two policies, which tie on profit under full compliance, end 6.1% apart. For drivers, disclosure raises income in the small model under both policies and LLMs; for users, it raises the service rate there by 10 to 18 percentage points. In Manhattan, self-interested drivers also make A a win-win-win against full compliance, raising driver income, platform profit and service rate by 10 to 12% each. Rebalancing policies that perform equally well under full compliance can thus show opposite results under mandatory disclosure. The study offers a framework to evaluate such policies under the new requirement and is, to our knowledge, the first to do so with LLM agents.

items.title: TensorSSM: Memorizing Spatial Position in Dynamic State Space for Tensor Core Generation
items.summary: arXiv:2610.40871v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: High-dimensional tensors are ubiquitous in real-world applications but lead to massive storage overhead. Functional tensor decomposition addresses this by employing neural networks to map element coordinates to tensor cores, significantly reducing the parameters for data compression. However, existing functional methods typically flatten high-order tensors into 1D sequences. This folding operation causes highly overlapping local coordinate sequences and struggles to capture complex cross-mode spatial dependencies, severely limiting their expressiveness on diverse datasets. To tackle these challenges, we propose TensorSSM, a novel Implicit Neural Representation (INR) for functional decomposition method that memorizes spatial positions within a dynamic State Space Model (SSM). Specifically, TensorSSM first decomposes mode-wise coordinates into sequences spit by K-ary rule, encoding spatial tokens from coarse to fine, which effectively captures spatial variations. Furthermore, we extend the SSM's state space to explicitly map cross-mode spatial dependencies, allowing inter-mode interactions to enhance the updates of each mode. By integrating cross-mode information from previous hidden states into the current state transitions, TensorSSM effectively expands tensor representation along two dimensions: the sequence dimension for coarse-to-fine spatial tokens, and the state dimension for cross-mode memorization. This design effectively integrates spatial information into the state space and the tensor core, substantially advancing the state adaptability and enhancing the expressiveness of the data compression. Extensive experiments demonstrate that TensorSSM achieves significantly high reconstruction accuracy and storage efficiency, exhibiting robust expressiveness across diverse tensor datasets without relying on strict spatial assumptions.

items.title: PDRVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Physical Dynamics Representations
items.summary: arXiv:2610.37381v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Vision--Language--Action (VLA) models generate robot actions from visual observations and language instructions, but their understanding of physical dynamics remains limited. Video world models can capture scene dynamics, yet generating future videos introduces high latency into the control loop. We introduce PDRVLA, whose lightweight Physical Dynamics Module extracts physical tokens from vision--language features to condition action generation without online video generation. The module learns through direct prediction of future RGB, depth, and optical-flow features, with auxiliary supervision through a frozen pretrained video world model. Training relies entirely on publicly available data, expanded through human-to-robot synthesis, subtask annotation, and embodied chain-of-thought (ECoT) annotation. Across four simulation benchmarks, PDRVLA achieves success rates of 99.3% on LIBERO, 89.9% on LIBERO-Plus, 93.6% on RoboTwin~2.0, and 81.5% on SimplerEnv. Ablations show improved future prediction with world-model supervision and evaluate how subtask conditioning, future object-pose supervision, and ECoT training affect action success.

items.title: Tactus: Tactile & Pose Sensing Glove for Natural Dexterity Data Collection
items.summary: arXiv:2610.39076v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Collecting naturalistic human manipulation demonstrations with accurate contact force and hand pose is essential for robot dexterous manipulation policy and foundational world model learning - yet no existing wearable platform provides both calibrated fingertip force sensing and occlusion-resilient hand tracking in a form factor that preserves natural manipulation behavior. We present Tactus, a textile-integrated sensing glove that co-optimizes three design pillars: (1) a thin, conformal 3D-knit form factor (1.5 mm fingertip stackup) designed to minimize interference with natural manipulation, (2) strategically placed capacitive tactile sensors at manipulation-relevant regions informed by empirical contact studies, and (3) IMU-fused pose tracking that maintains accuracy through the hand-object occlusions where manipulation data is most valuable. Tactus includes a documented calibration pipeline for cross-glove consistency and per-session calibration for subject-dependent correction. To enable objective comparison, we introduce standardized benchmarking protocols for tactile force regression and hand pose estimation, and apply them to Tactus and two commercially available tactile gloves - to our knowledge the first quantitative cross-platform evaluation of this kind. Tactus resolves a minimum detectable force of 0.59 N at 95% confidence, 1.6 - 2.7x lower than the commercial baselines, and with 0.87 cross-participant consistency, while our pose tracking sustains 11.0 mm fingertip keypoint relative error during manipulation, when occlusion is heaviest. We show that these combined signals support object property estimation, slip detection, and representative recording of hand-object interaction - yielding demonstration data with the fidelity required for contact-aware manipulation policies and world models.

items.title: 🎬 CUDA Rust: NVIDIA дала писать ядра для GPU на Rust и собирать их прямо в PTX
items.summary: CUDA Rust: NVIDIA дала писать ядра для GPU на Rust и собирать их прямо в PTX 🎯 NVIDIA выпустила CUDA Rust: теперь ядро для видеокарты пишут на Rust и компилируют в PTX, без обёртки вокруг чужого кода. Веток две под разные задачи. ⚙️ cuda-oxide повторяет модель SIMT: вы описываете работу одного потока, а карта запускает тысячи. Компилятор свой, на rustc: функции с пометкой kernel идут через MIR и LLVM. Нужны Linux, карта 8.0 и выше, CUDA 12 и ночная сборка Rust. Проект пока в ранней альфе. 🧱 cutile-rs работает плитками: вы говорите, что сделать с куском данных, а раскладку по потокам выбирает компилятор. Нужны стабильный Rust 1.89 и CUDA 13.3. Пакет на crates.io , его используют Grout и mistral.rs . 💡 Обе ветки ранние: покрытие неполное, API меняется. За контроль платят свободой: в плитках нет общей памяти и индексов потоков, а в SIMT общая память пока требует unsafe. Совместимость с CUDA C++ и CUDA Python обещают. Репозитории: cuda-oxide и cutile-rs . Rust теперь будет везде, походу. #CUDA #Rust #GPU #NVIDIA ------ @tsingular

items.title: Есть такой забавный подход как синтетическое пред-предобучение, когда модель обу...
items.summary: Есть такой забавный подход как синтетическое пред-предобучение, когда модель обучают на какой-то структурированной синтетике (клеточные автоматы, языки с балансированными вложенными скобками и т.п.), чтобы она заранее усвоила какие-то потенциально полезные структуры. Так вот, свежая работа показывает, что если честно учитывать все токены и флопсы, это ничего не даёт. Как только начинается обучение на естественном языке, оно нафиг перетирает все эти внедрённые баесы на правильные. Вспоминается анекдот про то, как потом пришёл муж и переделал всё по-своему. Ещё из забавного, это неплохо перекликается с работой этого года про то, что человеки используют неиерархические репрезентации языка там, где раньше думали про иерархические. Rethinking Pre-Pretraining Alexander Stern, Tim Rocktäschel, Acyr Locatelli, Laura Ruis Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.40051 Code: https://github.com/alexkstern/rethinking-ppt , https://github.com/alexkstern/llmtuna-hpo Review: https://arxiviq.substack.com/p/rethinking-pre-pretraining ЧТО сделали: Проверили, помогает ли синтетическое пред-предобучение (PPT) — предварительный этап обучения на процедурно сгенерированных последовательностях — при фиксированном бюджете FLOPs. Предложили синтетический корпус для поиска значений переменных DeclRef и оптимизатор гиперпараметров на базе LLM LLMTuna . ЧТО получили: Ни в одном из протестированных режимов с равным бюджетом вычислений PPT не обыгрывает обучение чисто на естественном языке. При дефиците данных (100M токенов FineWeb, 1 × 10¹⁸ FLOPs) повторение обычного текста даёт 1.064 бит на байт (BPB) на валидации, а выделение 1%–10% FLOPs на PPT ухудшает метрику до 1.068–1.076 BPB. При воспроизведении PPT на клеточных автоматах (NCA) для LLaMA на 400M параметров (OpenWebText) смена инициализации эмбеддингов с 𝒩(0, 1) на 𝒩(0, 0.02) улучшает перплексию бейзлайна без PPT на 9.0%, полностью перекрывая 5.4% выигрыша от NCA PPT. ПОЧЕМУ это важно: Предварительная подача синтетики впустую тратит вычисления: при переходе к естественному языку модель перезаписывает выученные структуры, а прежние успехи PPT во многом компенсировали плохую инициализацию весов. Впрочем, все модели здесь меньше 1B параметров, а тест инициализации LLaMA и эксперименты с перемешиванием данных проводились без повторного подбора гиперпараметров. Отказываться от синтетики тут: https://t.me/gonzo_ML_podcasts/4844 arXiv.org Rethinking Pre-pretraining We report that allocating compute to synthetic pre-pretraining (PPT) never outperforms pure natural-language training in our compute-matched experiments. items.title: Чуть выше в канале я писал про внутренний прогноз роста выручки Anthropic, и что он не п...
items.summary: Чуть выше в канале я писал про внутренний прогноз роста выручки Anthropic, и что он не подразумевает увеличения темпов роста в ближайшие кварталы. Их планирование исходит из того, что рост замедлится, и что кварталы с ростом на 100 и более процентов не повторятся. Но рост всё равно будет. Из обновленной S-1, как Паша писал выше, стало известно, что до конца 2030 года у Anthropic заключены контракты на $447b, или в среднем по $105B в год — это включая те, из которых они могут выйти. ChatGPT оценивает (так как точной цифры нет), что неотменяемые контракты в этот срок составляют не более $350B, или $82B в год. А на ближайшие 12 месяцев и того меньше — $65.5B неотменяемых и $70B в общем. Выручка за последний квартал — $17B, то есть даже если она перестанет расти (и не упадет), то в следующий год Anthropic получат $68B — этого хватит, чтобы оплатить все обязательства. Кроме этого есть другие операционные расходы, конечно, при темпе Q3 это будет ~$30B/год, из которых ~$18.5B — денежные, то есть придется жечь баланс. На балансе у компании более $120 миллиардов, и ещё $80-100B прибавится после IPO. Это я всё к чему. В обсуждениях последних дней люди достаточно часто как бы насмехаются над теми, кто говорит про выручку в ближайший год: • вы и дальше линии на графике просто вверх продолжаете? • ты правда думаешь что если они заработали $32B за 9 месяцев 2026-го, то за следующие 12 месяцев заработают около $70B? • и другие схожие вещи И поэтому даже такой простой тезис, как «Anthropic полностью или почти полностью смогут оплатить вычислительные мощности со своей выручки на горизонте 12 месяцев» вызывает вопросы и встречается скептиками в штыки — хотя как я расписал выше по сути это данность, предполагающая отсутствие любого дальнейшего роста. В попытках понять, насколько аналитики и скептики согласны со мной, я обратился к GPT и попросил поискать прогнозы «медведей» (так в финансах называют тех, кто верит в падение цены активов). Не буду детально пересказывать результаты , саммари такое: даже пессимистичные сценарии рассматривают, что рост какой-никакой будет. Кто-то считает, что через 4 квартала он опустится до полпроцента (но всё равно как-никак вырастет в предыдущие 3), кто-то даже рисует «скромные» десятки процентов роста. Отдельно хотел отметить прогноз FutureSearch — это как раз одна из систем ИИ-прогнозирования, про которую я пересылал сообщение выше. На недавних соревнованиях они обошли ведущих прогнозистов-людей. По мнению системы, уже к маю выручка Anthropic вырастет на 65% (не за год, а к маю!), а пессимистичный десятый перцентиль предсказания — на 25%. «Десятый перцентиль» означает, что 90% сценариев по построенной модели выходят лучше (выручка выше). Так что даже скептичные сценарии развития указывают на то, что Anthropic сможет оплатить мощности в ближайшие 12 месяцев со своей выручки, не сжигая деньги с баланса.

items.title: Жизнь после Claude Code: как я переехал на Codex и сохранил историю проектов
items.summary: В конце октября я неожиданно остался без рабочего Claude Code. После запроса на подтверждение личности Anthropic приостановила доступ к моей платной организации. Подписку Claude Max 20x впоследствии отменили, а в возврате средств отказали. Апелляцию я отправил, но разработку проектов останавливать на неопределённый срок не хотелось. Проблема оказалась не столько в выборе другой нейросети. За время работы с Claude Code накопились десятки проектов и диалогов. В них оставались архитектурные решения, обсуждения функций, результаты экспериментов, исправления ошибок, планы развития и множество мелочей, которые не всегда попадали в документацию. Исходный код никуда не исчез. Git-репозитории тоже. Но как объяснить новому агенту, почему проект устроен именно так, какие варианты мы уже отвергли и на чём остановились вчера? Я решил перейти на OpenAI Codex. Сначала задумался о собственном инструменте переноса истории, затем попробовал встроенный импорт Codex, но результат меня не устроил. В итоге обнаружил Hansard — инструмент, который не только позволяет восстанавливать историю работы в разных ИИ-агентах, но и предлагает дополнительные возможности для хранения, поиска и повторного использования накопленного контекста. items.title: Как заставить модель gemma-4-12B‑it QAT почти «летать» на ноутбучной RTX 2000 Ada, сохранив холод и тишину
items.summary: Уже несколько месяцев я активно экспериментирую с локальными языковыми моделями на своем ноутбуке Lenovo ThinkPad P16 Gen 2 (Intel Core i7-13850HX, 128 GB RAM, Samsung 980 Pro 2 TB + 990 Pro 1 TB). Конфигурация очень бодрая для любых задач, кроме… работы с тяжелыми ИИ-моделями. И узкое горлышко здесь очевидно - видеокарта Nvidia RTX 2000 Ada Laptop всего с 8 ГБ VRAM. Дискретная, быстрая, заточенная под ИИ, но видеопамяти катастрофически мало! Тем не менее даже в эти 8 гигабайт вполне можно уместить отличную локальную модель, да еще и с контекстом на 8192 токена. Это позволяет вести долгие осмысленные диалоги без потери нити обсуждения. После долгих поисков и тестов я остановился на одной модели - gemma-4-12B-it-QAT в квантовании q4_0. Почему именно она? Премиальный уровень «из коробки»: Это модель от Google, обученная на их топовых решениях. Метод QAT (Quantization-Aware Training) минимизирует потери качества при «упаковке» в 4 бита. Минимум галлюцинаций: При правильной настройке (особенно с немного заниженной температурой) модель отлично держит контекст и выдает точные энциклопедические данные. Срез знаний у нее свежий “конец 2025 - начало 2026 года”. Настоящая локальная «мини-Википедия»! Хороший кодинг: Модель отлично пишет код (особенно на Python и PowerShell). Последующая верификация в среде разработки проходит практически со 100%-й точностью. Идеально влезает в VRAM: Вместе с контекстом в 8192 токена она целиком помещается в 8 ГБ видеопамяти. В LM Studio на моем ноутбуке она выдает честные 12 токенов в секунду, чего более чем достаточно для комфортного диалога. Читать далее

items.title: 🖼 Anthropic выпустили в опенсорс FlashProve – инструмент для доказуемого инференса
items.summary: Anthropic выпустили в опенсорс FlashProve – инструмент для доказуемого инференса https://github.com/anthropics/FlashProve По сути они предложили прототип открытого криптографического протокола, через который любой проверяющий без доступа к весам может убедиться, что ответ выдала именно та модель, которая была заявлена провайдером. Нужна такая штука например для того, чтобы проверять, что роутинг-сервис не подменяет модель на более дешевую, или что модель в контуре компании не была заменена злоумышленниками. Работает это так: провайдер заранее публикует цифровую печать своих весов, а к каждому ответу затем прикладывает файл-доказательство. Мэтч этого файла и печати означает подлинность модели, и проверить его можно на обычном компьютере без GPU и весов. Доказательство весит около 19 МБ на запрос в 1024 токена, а проверка занимает около 17 секунд. Понятно, что это все еще в разы дороже обычного инференса, но, для сравнения, предыдущий результат составлял около 14 часов проверки и доказательство на 93 ГБ. Алгоритм основан на методе zkSNARK. Он известен достаточно давно, но заслуга Anthropic именно в том, что они смогли оптимизировать его до практичных скоростей на модели до 400В параметров. Кстати, в статье написано , что ускорением и оптимизацией в основном занимался Claude. Может быть так и до детектора происхождения текстов недалеко

items.title: Искусственный интеллект как система управления. Как государства, спецслужбы и мошенники манипулируют вашим сознанием
items.summary: Вы когда-нибудь задумывались о том, можно ли использовать машинное обучение не только для слежки и бизнеса, но и для управления людьми? Можно ли получить власть над разумом человека и заставить его думать и желать, говорить и действовать так, как нужно манипулятору? Словно это были его собственные мысли и убеждения, которые он, разумеется, будет искренне защищать и оправдывать. Более того, будет готов понести реальные утраты (время, ресурсы, здоровье), попускаясь своей личной выгодой и настоящими интересами даже не осознавая этого. Кем бы вы ни были, скептиком или параноиком, специалистом или обывателем, я настоятельно прошу уделить статье немного вашего драгоценного времени. Если оно было потрачено зря, влепите ей минус, но прочтите. Это все о чем я вас прошу! В этой статья я изложу теорию управления субъектами и причем тут машинное обучение. Она поможет вам осознать манипулирование со стороны структур, а так же повысит вашу подготовленность к разным ситуациям, например при столкновении с мошенниками. Вместо разбора конкретный кейсов, которые ничего не дадут, ибо все слишком индивидуально, вас ждут основы технологии эксплуатации личностных черт. Можно сказать, что это небольшой треннинг с множеством примеров и практикой. Такие умения словно иммунитет, помогут вам в жизни, особенно сегодня, когда ИИ все лучше учится взламывать человеческий разум. В конце вас ждет набор рекомендаций. Читать далее
